You are reviewing candidate defect findings against a fixed snapshot of Rust
production source code. The source is under sources/. The findings are in
01-findings.json, identified only by content-addressed finding_id values.

You do not know what system produced the findings. Do not guess or state their
origin. Judge each finding only against the source code. Your judgment is
non-authoritative review evidence and does not verify a defect or authorize an
issue, patch, or other repository change.

Read all findings and every referenced source range. For every finding_id,
return exactly one judgment:

- disposition is issue_should_be_created when the mechanism is plausible or
  confirmed and actionable; should_not_be_created when it is likely false,
  intended, unsupported, or non-actionable; unable_to_determine only when the
  available source is genuinely insufficient.
- duplicate_of lists other finding IDs with the same underlying defect.
- specificity reports whether the cited file and lines exist and are relevant.
- unresolvable_location is true only when a path or range does not exist.
- reproduction_conditions_stated is true only for a concrete trigger.
- false_positive_suspected and design_intent_confusion_suspected record those
  concerns independently of disposition.
- notes gives concise source-based reasoning without discussing origin.

Return only the JSON object required by the supplied output schema. Include no
Markdown or commentary outside it. Set unit_id to m18-debate-r1.
{
  "schema": "reviewgraphen.benchmark.m17_blind_findings.v1",
  "unit_id": "m18-debate-r1",
  "findings": [
    {
      "finding_id": "finding:586b797389f0e84407da0fd73bae4f9b",
      "locations": [
        {
          "path": "rust/fsl-core/src/compose.rs",
          "start_line": 585,
          "end_line": 740
        },
        {
          "path": "rust/fsl-core/src/compose.rs",
          "start_line": 741,
          "end_line": 855
        }
      ],
      "mechanism_tags": [],
      "severity": "medium",
      "rationale": "Let arm in rewrite_action_items does not extend bound, unlike all other binder forms. rewrite_action_items (609-631) processes each ActionItem independently via .map with the same immutable bound reference; the Let arm (623-625) rewrites only the initializer expression and never inserts the bound name into bound. This contrasts with rewrite_binder (844-855), Expr::Quantified (796-802), and Expr::Aggregate (810-816), which all clone bound and insert the binder name before rewriting the body. The .map structure makes per-item bound extension impossible without restructuring the function, and Let is an ActionItem rather than a Statement, so there is no other path that would add its name to bound. Effect: if a let-bound name matches a component state or const name, a subsequent item's rvalue reference to that name is still rewritten by rewrite_expr's Var arm (711-717) to alias.name (the state/const) because !bound.contains(&name) still holds, rather than resolving to the local binding. Reachability and intent caveats: whether the surface grammar permits a let name to shadow a state/const name is not established in the projections; whether the intended scoping semantics is local-binding-wins is an interpretation rather than a projected fact; and the encoding of the subsequent reference as Expr::Var is assumed from the description rather than shown in a projection."
    },
    {
      "finding_id": "finding:8532e50a62439b9b955d6d619a6f3947",
      "locations": [
        {
          "path": "rust/fsl-core/src/compose.rs",
          "start_line": 585,
          "end_line": 740
        }
      ],
      "mechanism_tags": [],
      "severity": "high",
      "rationale": "Lvalue rewrite ignores the bound set, creating asymmetric qualification between lvalue and rvalue for shadowed names. rewrite_lvalue (687-698) routes LValue::Var and LValue::Index names through rewrite_state_name (700-706), which prefixes any name in component.names.state without consulting bound; bound is applied only to the Index sub-expression via rewrite_expr, never to the variable name itself. This is asymmetric with rewrite_statement's ForAll arm (670-683), which clones bound and inserts the binder before rewriting the body, and with rewrite_expr's Var arm (711-717), which guards qualification on !bound.contains(&name). Effect: within a ForAll (or Quantified/Aggregate) body whose binder name matches a component state name, an assignment or index target to that name is still prefixed to alias.x by rewrite_state_name while the identical name in the rvalue is left bare by rewrite_expr, producing alias.x := f(x) instead of the intended x := f(x). Reachability caveat: whether the surface grammar permits a binder to shadow a component state name is not established in the available projections; if shadowing is illegal, this asymmetry is latent rather than triggerable. The downstream kernel behavior for the mixed qualification is not in the projections, so the kernel-corruption consequence is inferred from the immediate qualification split rather than observed."
    },
    {
      "finding_id": "finding:878e86268579d0be179f2ace00ff4c35",
      "locations": [
        {
          "path": "rust/fsl-core/src/compose.rs",
          "start_line": 585,
          "end_line": 740
        },
        {
          "path": "rust/fsl-core/src/compose.rs",
          "start_line": 741,
          "end_line": 855
        }
      ],
      "mechanism_tags": [],
      "severity": "medium",
      "rationale": "Non-exhaustive rewrite_expr/rewrite_type catch-alls (other => other) silently pass unhandled variants through without qualification. rewrite_expr ends in `other => other` (840) and rewrite_type ends in `other => other` (589): any Expr/TypeExpr variant not explicitly enumerated is returned unchanged, with no qualification of embedded identifiers and no compile-time exhaustiveness error. Trigger: any fall-through variant carrying unqualified state/const/type names (including variants added later) yields unresolvable references in the lowered kernel; the catch-all makes the omission silent. Expr::Call likewise leaves its name unqualified (742-749), which is sound only if call names are always global."
    }
  ]
}
